proposals: The Department of Expenditure should publish with each Budget a commodity-wise statement of the cost of holding domestic prices below import parity for fuels, fertilisers and edible oils, so the ₹2.2–2.8 lakh crore burden is an official figure rather than a range estimated from outside.

The Department of Fertilizers should publish monthly import volumes, average landed prices and subsidy paid per tonne for urea and DAP, so a jump like the 76 per cent rise in the fertiliser import bill can be split into price and quantity effects.

The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare should publish a yearly NMEO-Oilseeds progress statement giving domestic edible-oil output and the self-sufficiency ratio against the 72 per cent target for 2030, so progress from 43 per cent can be checked against the import trend.

DPIIT should publish PLI disbursement scheme by scheme alongside the HS chapters each scheme is meant to substitute, so the roughly 18 per cent disbursal rate can be read against import growth in each chapter, and chapters with no scheme, such as plastics, are visible on the same page.
